plugin-lifecycle.reason: No plugin load/teardown or IDA callbacks change; the RAX process backend remains behind its existing entry points.

UI-state.reason: No Qt widgets, ownership, rendering or copy changes.

conversation-lane.reason: No transcript, cancellation, lane or history implementation changes.

agent-backend.reason: Native/ACP orchestration and provider requests do not consume the private token metadata.

prompt-context.reason: No prompts, context collection or anonymization changes.

tool-schema.reason: Existing emulation options and result schemas remain unchanged; no new tool is registered.

permission-mutation.reason: Token reads retain measured TOKEN_QUERY grants and rejection ordering. No guest token mutation or host-call forwarding is added.

main-thread-dispatch.reason: The Rust userland engine calls no IDA, Hex-Rays or Qt API.

mesh-MCP.reason: No routing, identity, discovery manifest or external protocol change.

transport-crypto.reason: No framing, credentials or cryptographic data changes.

persistence.reason: Captured properties are private to one process runtime; no persisted schema or path changes.

SDK-ABI.reason: The new map is internal Rust state. No exported C layout, function signature or ABI version changes.

optional-engines.reason: RAX gains native scalar token-query semantics through the existing userland backend. Z3 and other engines are unchanged.

update-release.reason: The eventual RAX pin and engineering records must be paired. No package layout, defaults, dependency or release automation change is intended.

targets-platforms.reason: Shared query/model code compiled and ran on macOS, Linux and Windows; the narrow Windows acquisition adapter ran on Windows ARM64. Core and retained C API/Assist consumers were verified separately. Four native caller profiles share one ARM64 kernel; physical x64-kernel and whole-current-root package validation are not claimed.

tests-docs.reason: Native matrices, both focused epochs, full three-host gates, exact artifacts and retained application outcomes are recorded.
